purpose: session_bounded_stepwise_execution_for selecting, computing, validating, and responsibly reporting research impact indicators (journal metrics, altmetrics, field-normalized and percentile citation impact, productivity, societal/economic impact) for defensible research evaluation
assumptions: subdomain of bibliometrics, scientometrics & research evaluation
no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
evaluation is decision-oriented and must respect responsible-metrics frameworks
nodes are concrete work units/methods/decision areas within research impact measurement
exclusions: peer-review process design beyond metric use
general statistics theory not specific to impact metrics
research funding allocation mechanics beyond impact assessment

competency_questions.question: How is the evaluation question, unit of analysis, comparison set, and time window specified before any metric is selected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: trace from SCOPE_QUESTION_FRAMING outputs to a scoping document

competency_questions.question: Which field/document-type/time normalization basis makes counts comparable across disciplines and over time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNIT_NORMALIZATION_BASIS specifies the basis used by FIELD_NORMALIZED_CITATION and LONGITUDINAL_TREND_DYNAMICS

competency_questions.question: What baseline turns a normalized value into an above/below-average interpretation?
Which bibliographic data source is chosen, what are its coverage limits, and how is reproducibility ensured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATA_SOURCE_SELECTION outputs a source decision record with coverage gaps; REPRODUCIBILITY_AUDIT packages it

competency_questions.question: How are journal-level metrics (JIF, SJR, SNIP, Eigenfactor, CiteScore, 5-year IF) computed and contrasted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JOURNAL_IMPACT_FACTOR and ALT_JOURNAL_METRICS produce a multi-metric journal profile

competency_questions.question: Why should journal metrics not be used to evaluate individual articles or authors?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JIF cons + responsible-metrics constraints prohibit author-level inference

competency_questions.question: How are usage and altmetric attention signals captured and bounded against quality claims?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USAGE_METRICS and ALTMETRICS_ATTENTION produce profiles with quality caveats

competency_questions.question: How is societal/policy/economic reach beyond academia captured and evidenced with contribution/attribution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ALTMETRICS_ATTENTION and SOCIETAL_ECONOMIC_IMPACT provide policy/impact evidence with contribution analysis

competency_questions.question: How are field-normalized (MNCS) and percentile/top-x% citation impacts computed and which is more robust to skew?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_NORMALIZED_CITATION and PERCENTILE_TOPX are paired; percentile is skew-robust

competency_questions.question: How are productivity vs impact composites and defensible researcher/group profiles (with disambiguation and credit) computed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRODUCTIVITY_COMPOSITES and RESEARCHER_LEVEL_PROFILING with normalization, disambiguation, and credit allocation

competency_questions.question: Which responsible-metrics frameworks (Leiden, DORA, Metric Tide) constrain indicator use and how are they operationalized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESPONSIBLE_METRICS_FRAMEWORKS maps each principle to an enforced rule

competency_questions.question: How is a fit-for-purpose multi-indicator portfolio assembled, tied to the question, and reported with uncertainty and responsible-use statements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDICATOR_SELECTION_PORTFOLIO maps indicators to facets; REPORTING_INTERPRETATION integrates uncertainty and constraints

competency_questions.question: How is the construct/convergent/predictive validity of each indicator assessed against its intended construct?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METRIC_VALIDITY_ASSESSMENT links each indicator to the construct it measures

competency_questions.question: How are gaming and Goodhart effects anticipated and detected once a metric becomes a high-stakes target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METRIC_GAMING_GOODHART enumerates gaming vectors and detection thresholds

glossary.definition: journal impact factor: mean 2-year citations per citable item
mean normalized citation score relative to a field+year+doctype baseline
share of a unit's papers in the top 10% most-cited of their field/year
non-citation attention/usage traces from social, news, policy, and platform sources
frameworks (DORA, Leiden, Metric Tide) constraining how indicators may be used
degradation of a measure's validity once it becomes a high-stakes target
largest h such that h papers each have at least h citations
the field/doctype/window scheme defining reference sets for comparison
degree to which an indicator measures the construct it is used to assess
research effects on society, economy, policy, or practice beyond academia

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors over research impact metrics, scientometrics, and research evaluation drawn from established methodology (e.g., de Solla Price 1963; Moed 2005; Ding, Rousseau & Wolfram 2014; Leiden Manifesto; DORA; Metric Tide) without an observed dataset
grounding_limits: scores are heuristic priors, not measured values

nodes.definition: Specify the evaluation question, unit (article/researcher/group/journal/country), comparison set, and time window before any metric is chosen.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation purpose or decision stakes change

pros.claim: frame fixes the comparison set that makes any metric interpretable
pros.example: ranking departments needs a same-field, same-window frame

cons.claim: over-broad framing invites metric shopping later
cons.example: asking 'who is best' without a field/window frame

acceptance_tests: scoping document names unit, comparison set, window, and decision
no indicator selected before frame approved

nodes.definition: Choose the field/document-type/time normalization basis that makes counts comparable across disciplines and ages.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: field classification scheme or citation-window convention revised

pros.claim: normalization basis controls cross-field comparability of every downstream metric
pros.example: MNCS uses field+year+doctype reference sets

cons.claim: field delineation is arbitrary at boundaries and changes ranks
cons.example: interdisciplinary papers sit between fields

failure_modes: mono-disciplinary scheme applied to interdisciplinary output
too-short citation window for slow fields
acceptance_tests: boundary cases of field assignment audited

nodes.definition: Select and reconcile bibliographic data source(s) (WoS, Scopus, Dimensions, OpenAlex, Crossref) whose coverage and identifiers underpin all counts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: source coverage materially changes (new index, dedup policy)

pros.claim: source coverage and field bias dictate which metrics are defensible
pros.example: WoS undercounts non-English and book output

cons.claim: each source has different coverage, inflating or deflating counts
cons.example: Scopus vs WoS produce different h-indices

nodes.definition: Compute and interpret JIF: citations in year Y to a journal's citable items of years Y-1,Y-2 divided by that item count.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: JCR methodology or citable-item rule changes

pros.claim: JIF is the most recognized journal signal and drives indexing/subscription decisions
pros.example: JCR quartiles gate journal selection

cons.claim: skewed citation distributions make the mean a poor central tendency
cons.example: a few highly-cited papers carry the JIF

failure_modes: JIF used to evaluate individual articles or authors
acceptance_tests: JIF reported with distribution not as point estimate
no author-level inference drawn from JIF

nodes.definition: Compute and contrast SJR, SNIP, Eigenfactor, CiteScore, and 5-year IF as prestige/field-normalized/window-varied journal indicators.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: SNIP/SJR algorithm or source database revised

pros.claim: field-normalized and prestige-weighted metrics correct JIF's cross-field bias
pros.example: SNIP enables comparing chemistry and math journals

cons.claim: each algorithm encodes different assumptions producing divergent ranks
cons.example: SJR and Eigenfactor can disagree on the same journal

failure_modes: source-database mismatch (Scopus SJR vs WoS JIF)
acceptance_tests: at least one field-normalized journal metric reported alongside JIF

nodes.definition: Quantify download/view/readership usage signals (COUNTER usage, Mendeley readers) as early, pre-citation impact proxies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: COUNTER standard revised or platform usage definition changes

pros.claim: usage signals appear before citations, giving early impact estimates
pros.example: downloads weakly predict later citations early

cons.claim: usage is easily gamed and platform-dependent
cons.example: bot downloads inflate counts

failure_modes: raw usage compared across platforms with different counting

nodes.definition: Capture and interpret attention from social media, news, blogs, and policy documents as non-citation impact traces.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: altmetric provider changes source coverage or scoring weights

pros.claim: captures societal/policy reach invisible to citations
pros.example: policy-document citation evidences real-world uptake

cons.claim: attention is not quality and is highly skewed and gameable
cons.example: viral controversy inflates a weak paper's score

failure_modes: attention conflated with quality or impact
weighted composite (AAS) treated as a measurement
acceptance_tests: source-type breakdown reported, not just composite score

nodes.definition: Compute field- and age-normalized citation impact such as MNCS / category-normalized citation impact (CNCI) relative to a world/reference baseline.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reference-set or field-delineation method revised

pros.claim: removes field and age bias, enabling cross-discipline comparison
pros.example: MNCS=1.5 means 50% above world average for field+year

cons.claim: unstable for small samples and sensitive to field delineation
cons.example: few papers in a niche field give volatile MNCS

failure_modes: MNCS reported for very small sample without uncertainty
reference set mismatched to publication year

nodes.definition: Compute percentile-based and top-x% (PPtop10%) indicators that are robust to skew by ranking papers within field/year strata.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: percentile binning or tie-handling convention changes

pros.claim: robust to the heavy skew of citation distributions
pros.example: PPtop10% is stable where mean MNCS is volatile

cons.claim: tie-handling and binning choices change results at thresholds
cons.example: many uncited papers create ties at low percentiles

nodes.definition: Compute productivity and productivity-vs-impact composites (publication counts, h-index, g-index, m-quotient) and their limitations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: career-stage or field-size confounds re-examined

pros.claim: single-number summaries are easy to communicate and rank
pros.example: h-index combines output and impact

cons.claim: confounds career length and field size; field-uncomparable
cons.example: senior researchers always outscore juniors on h

failure_modes: h-index compared across fields/career stages without normalization

nodes.definition: Apply responsible-metrics frameworks (Leiden Manifesto, DORA, Metric Tide) to constrain how indicators may be used in evaluation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: framework updated or institutional policy adopts new principles

pros.claim: constrains misuse and aligns metrics with evaluation purpose
pros.example: DORA bans JIF in hiring/promotion

cons.claim: principles are aspirational and hard to operationalize/enforce
cons.example: Leiden principles conflict with ranking pressure

failure_modes: framework cited but not operationalized into constraints
metrics used contrary to adopted policy
acceptance_tests: each adopted principle mapped to an enforced indicator-use rule

nodes.definition: Assess construct, convergent, and predictive validity of each indicator against the evaluation question it is meant to inform.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence emerges that indicator measures a different construct than assumed

pros.claim: prevents using indicators that do not measure the intended construct
pros.example: citations measure attention, not quality

cons.claim: validity evidence is incomplete and contested for most indicators
cons.example: no metric fully captures 'research quality'

acceptance_tests: each indicator linked to the construct it validly measures

nodes.definition: Identify and mitigate gaming, Goodhart/Campbell effects, and manipulation (self/coercive citation, citation cartels, salami slicing) once a metric becomes a target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new gaming pattern observed or metric becomes high-stakes incentive

pros.claim: anticipates distortion when a metric becomes a target
pros.example: JIF chasing drives editorial coercive citation

cons.claim: detection lags novel gaming strategies
cons.example: citation cartels evolve faster than detectors

failure_modes: high-stakes metric deployed without gaming safeguards
acceptance_tests: gaming vectors enumerated per deployed metric

nodes.definition: Assess research impact beyond academia: societal, economic, clinical, environmental, and policy outcomes, often via narrative + evidence (e.g., REF impact case studies).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: impact-assessment framework or attribution method revised

pros.claim: captures the real-world value funders ultimately care about
pros.example: REF case studies evidence clinical guideline change

cons.claim: attribution and time-lag make causal claims weak; costly to assess
cons.example: impact may surface decades after the research

failure_modes: narrative impact reduced to a single score
acceptance_tests: impact claims supported by contribution/attribution evidence

nodes.definition: Assemble a fit-for-purpose multi-indicator portfolio matched to the evaluation question, avoiding single-metric reliance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation question changes or an indicator's validity is revised

pros.claim: triangulated portfolios resist single-metric distortion
pros.example: combine PPtop10%, MNCS, and qualitative review

cons.claim: aggregating heterogeneous indicators can hide tradeoffs
cons.example: a composite index obscures which dimension drives it

acceptance_tests: portfolio maps each indicator to a question facet
weights and aggregation justified or avoided

nodes.definition: Quantify uncertainty, sampling stability, and robustness (confidence intervals, bootstrap, small-N flags) of every reported indicator.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sample size or distributional assumptions change materially

pros.claim: intervals prevent overinterpreting unstable small-sample metrics
pros.example: bootstrap CIs reveal a rank tie is noise

cons.claim: uncertainty quantification is omitted in most reporting
cons.example: ranks shown to 3 decimals with no CI

acceptance_tests: every reported indicator carries an uncertainty interval

nodes.definition: Make the metric computation reproducible: documented queries, data snapshots, code, and versioned reference sets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data source snapshot or computation pipeline changes

pros.claim: reproducible packages let evaluations be audited and rerun
pros.example: snapshot + code reproduce the exact ranking

cons.claim: data snapshots age quickly; sources are often non-redistributable
cons.example: license blocks sharing the raw extract

failure_modes: results not reproducible from documented inputs
acceptance_tests: independent rerun reproduces results within tolerance

nodes.definition: Establish the world/field/peer baselines against which normalized and percentile indicators are calibrated and interpreted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reference period or peer-group definition changes

pros.claim: baselines turn raw normalized values into interpretable above/below-average claims
pros.example: MNCS>1 only means above average given the baseline

cons.claim: peer-group choice changes whether a unit looks above or below average
cons.example: shifting the comparison group flips the verdict

failure_modes: baseline implicit or mismatched to unit/window
peer group chosen to flatter results
acceptance_tests: baseline definition documented and matched to unit

nodes.definition: Produce the evaluation report that interprets the indicator portfolio with caveats, uncertainty, and responsible-use statements for decision-makers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: decision context changes or new evidence revises an indicator

pros.claim: decision-makers act on the report, so interpretation quality is decisive
pros.example: a caveated report prevents misuse of a single rank

cons.claim: clear single numbers are demanded but mislead without caveats
cons.example: stakeholders ignore caveats and quote the rank

failure_modes: report presents ranks without uncertainty or caveats
acceptance_tests: report ties every claim to the evaluation question

nodes.definition: Model temporal dynamics of impact: citation accrual curves, citation aging, delayed recognition ('sleeping beauties'), and trend comparison over windows.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: citation window convention or aging model changes

pros.claim: window choice strongly affects metrics; trends reveal what snapshots hide
pros.example: a short window penalizes slow-citing fields

cons.claim: trend models need long histories and stable indexing
cons.example: indexing changes confound apparent trends

failure_modes: fixed short window applied to slow-citing field
acceptance_tests: window choice justified against field citation-aging

nodes.definition: Build defensible researcher/group-level impact profiles that combine normalized indicators with name-disambiguation and co-authorship credit allocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: disambiguation method or credit-allocation policy changes

pros.claim: name disambiguation and credit allocation make author metrics defensible
pros.example: ORCID + fractional credit fixes homonym inflation

cons.claim: disambiguation errors and credit disputes propagate to high-stakes decisions
cons.example: two researchers sharing a name merge profiles

failure_modes: name homonyms merged or split incorrectly
acceptance_tests: disambiguation accuracy audited on a sample
human review of high-stakes individual profiles

edges.why_related: the evaluation unit and comparison frame determine which normalization basis is valid
edges.example: country comparison forces field-and-size normalization
edges.resolution_rule: fix frame before choosing normalization basis

edges.why_related: the question's scope drives source coverage requirements
edges.risk_of_conflict: coverage gap if source picked first
edges.example: humanities scope needs book-inclusive source
edges.resolution_rule: set scope before selecting data source

edges.why_related: the evaluation purpose determines which responsible-use principles apply
edges.risk_of_conflict: misuse if constraints set without purpose
edges.example: promotion use triggers DORA constraints
edges.resolution_rule: anchor responsible-use rules to evaluation purpose

edges.why_related: validity is assessed relative to the construct the question targets
edges.risk_of_conflict: validity untestable without a target construct
edges.example: assessing whether MNCS measures 'quality' needs the quality construct defined
edges.resolution_rule: define the target construct before validity assessment

edges.why_related: JIF requires JCR/WoS source data and item classification
edges.example: JIF needs JCR citable-item classification
edges.resolution_rule: fix source before computing JIF

edges.why_related: usage metrics require COUNTER/publisher logs from the chosen source
edges.risk_of_conflict: no usage data if source lacks logs
edges.example: COUNTER usage requires publisher feed
edges.resolution_rule: secure usage data source first

edges.why_related: MNCS requires citation data and reference sets from the chosen source
edges.example: MNCS from Scopus differs from WoS
edges.resolution_rule: lock source before computing field-normalized impact

edges.why_related: h-index and counts depend on source publication/citation coverage
edges.example: h-index higher in Google Scholar than WoS
edges.resolution_rule: fix source coverage before productivity indices

edges.why_related: trend analysis needs stable longitudinal coverage from the source
edges.example: coverage expansion mimics rising citations
edges.resolution_rule: verify longitudinal coverage stability first

edges.why_related: field-normalized impact is computed from the chosen normalization basis
edges.example: field+year+doctype reference set defines MNCS denominator
edges.resolution_rule: finalize normalization basis before MNCS

edges.why_related: percentile strata are defined by the field/year normalization basis
edges.example: PPtop10% computed within field+year cells
edges.resolution_rule: fix strata basis before percentile computation

edges.why_related: baselines are expected values derived from the normalization basis
edges.example: world baseline=1.0 is the field+year mean
edges.resolution_rule: set normalization basis before baseline calibration

edges.why_related: trend metrics depend on consistent windowing from the normalization basis
edges.example: comparing 2-yr vs 5-yr windows distorts trend
edges.resolution_rule: fix window basis before trend analysis

edges.why_related: computing JIF first frames the contrast with field-normalized journal metrics
edges.benefit_of_coupling: JIF baseline clarifies what alt metrics add
edges.risk_of_conflict: redundant work if computed in isolation
edges.example: show SNIP correcting JIF's field bias
edges.resolution_rule: compute JIF, then contrast with alternatives

edges.why_related: mean-based MNCS is naturally complemented by skew-robust percentile indicators
edges.risk_of_conflict: misleading if only one is shown
edges.example: MNCS=2 with low PPtop10% signals one outlier
edges.resolution_rule: report MNCS with percentile indicators

edges.why_related: validity assessment evaluates whether normalized citation impact measures the target construct
edges.example: does CNCI measure quality or just attention?
edges.resolution_rule: compute normalized impact before judging its validity

edges.why_related: responsible-metrics principles require validity evidence for any indicator used
edges.example: Leiden principle: support qualitative with quantitative
edges.resolution_rule: apply frameworks, then assess validity

edges.why_related: knowing what a metric validly measures is prerequisite to detecting gaming of it
edges.risk_of_conflict: cannot detect gaming without a valid baseline
edges.example: self-citation spike detectable against valid pattern
edges.resolution_rule: assess validity before modeling gaming

edges.why_related: responsible-use policy defines which high-stakes uses create gaming incentives to guard
edges.risk_of_conflict: blind gaming controls without policy scope
edges.example: DORA-banned JIF-in-hiring is the gaming surface to guard
edges.resolution_rule: set responsible-use policy before gaming controls

edges.why_related: only validated indicators may enter the portfolio
edges.example: drop an indicator that fails construct validity
edges.resolution_rule: validate indicators before portfolio assembly

edges.why_related: responsible-use constraints bound which indicators and aggregations are permitted
edges.example: no single JIF-based ranking for individuals
edges.resolution_rule: portfolio must satisfy responsible-use constraints

edges.why_related: robust percentile indicators are core candidates for the portfolio
edges.example: PPtop10% included as a stable indicator
edges.resolution_rule: have percentile indicators ready before portfolio

edges.why_related: uncertainty analysis quantifies the stability of the computed normalized impact
edges.example: small-N MNCS gets a wide bootstrap CI
edges.resolution_rule: compute indicators before their uncertainty

edges.why_related: percentile indicators need stability checks near threshold cuts
edges.example: a paper at the 10.5% boundary is unstable
edges.resolution_rule: test percentile stability after computing them

edges.why_related: productivity indices need uncertainty when comparing across confounded groups
edges.example: h-index difference within CI is not real
edges.resolution_rule: quantify uncertainty of productivity indices

edges.why_related: the calibrated baseline bounds how normalized values are interpreted
edges.example: MNCS=1.2 means 20% above the calibrated baseline
edges.resolution_rule: interpret normalized impact only against the baseline

edges.why_related: the report interprets the assembled indicator portfolio
edges.example: report explains each indicator's contribution
edges.resolution_rule: assemble portfolio before writing the report

edges.why_related: the report must present uncertainty alongside every indicator
edges.example: ranks shown with CIs, not as exact
edges.resolution_rule: finalize uncertainty before reporting

edges.why_related: the report must carry the responsible-use statement and honor use constraints
edges.example: report states metrics not for individual ranking
edges.resolution_rule: report must include responsible-use statement

edges.why_related: societal/economic impact evidence is integrated into the final report narrative
edges.example: REF case study added to the impact section
edges.resolution_rule: gather broader-impact evidence before reporting

edges.why_related: responsible frameworks legitimize and structure broader-impact assessment over pure bibliometrics
edges.example: Metric Tide endorses broader impact assessment
edges.resolution_rule: frame responsible use before broader-impact work

edges.why_related: the reproducibility package captures the assembled portfolio computations
edges.example: package includes portfolio queries and code
edges.resolution_rule: assemble portfolio before packaging it

edges.why_related: reproducibility requires the source data snapshot and access record
edges.example: store the WoS extract date and query
edges.resolution_rule: record source snapshot for reproducibility

edges.why_related: detected gaming can trigger revision of how results are reported and caveated
edges.example: flagged citation cartel adds a report caveat
edges.resolution_rule: stop when no further gaming flags change the interpretation; if gaming found, revise report

edges.why_related: report findings can reveal the original question was mis-scoped, triggering re-framing
edges.example: results show the comparison set was wrong
edges.resolution_rule: stop after one re-scope unless a new material scope defect appears

edges.why_related: field-normalized impact and raw productivity indices pull evaluation toward quality vs quantity
edges.example: high output low MNCS vs low output high MNCS
edges.resolution_rule: impact validity dominates; productivity is reported as context, not the verdict

edges.why_related: altmetric attention pressures inclusion despite weak construct validity for quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: attention treated as quality if unvalidated
edges.example: high AAS cited as evidence of impact quality
edges.resolution_rule: validity dominates; attention may enter only with an explicit, validated meaning

edges.why_related: gameable indicators pressure the portfolio; gaming risk competes with metric familiarity/recognition
edges.example: JIF kept for familiarity despite gaming risk
edges.resolution_rule: gaming risk dominates for high-stakes uses; drop or hard-guard gameable indicators

conflict_axes.trigger: evaluation rewards output volume at the expense of normalized impact
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validated impact dominates; productivity reported only as context
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: decision flips depending on whether output count or MNCS is weighted
conflict_axes.example: prolific author with low MNCS vs selective author with high MNCS

conflict_axes.trigger: high attention treated as evidence of research quality
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validity dominates; attention enters only with an explicit validated meaning
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an indicator is used as quality proxy without validity evidence
conflict_axes.example: a controversial paper with a high Altmetric score cited as 'impactful'

conflict_axes.trigger: a recognizable but gameable metric is retained for high-stakes use
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: gaming resistance dominates for high-stakes uses; drop or hard-guard gameable metrics
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a high-stakes use relies on a metric with known manipulation vectors
conflict_axes.example: keeping JIF for promotion despite coercive-citation risk

conflict_axes.trigger: stakeholders demand one number while validity needs triangulation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: portfolio/responsible-use dominates; provide a structured profile not a single rank
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a single ranking is requested for a high-stakes decision
conflict_axes.example: a league table reduced to one composite score

conflict_axes.trigger: deadline pressure pushes release before validity/uncertainty work completes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rigor dominates for high-stakes reports; validity and uncertainty gates must pass
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: report requested before uncertainty analysis is done
conflict_axes.example: publishing ranks without confidence intervals to meet a deadline

conflict_axes.trigger: adding sources to improve coverage breaks cross-unit comparability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: comparability dominates within a comparison; one consistent basis per comparison set
conflict_axes.example: comparing a Scopus-based unit to a WoS-based unit

conflict_axes.trigger: a short citation window penalizes slow-citing fields
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: window must match field citation-aging; do not impose a single short window across fields
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a 2-year window applied to mathematics and biomedicine alike
conflict_axes.example: math journals look weak under a 2-year JIF window

conflict_axes.trigger: license terms forbid sharing the raw extract needed for full reproducibility
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: share maximal reproducible artifacts within license; document what cannot be shared
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: raw data cannot be redistributed under the source license
conflict_axes.example: sharing queries and code but not the proprietary citation extract

conflict_axes.trigger: indicators valid at aggregate level are pushed onto individual high-stakes decisions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: responsible-use dominates; individual decisions require validated individual-level evidence and human review
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an aggregate-valid metric is decisive in a single hiring case
conflict_axes.example: using department-level MNCS to deny one person tenure

edge_cases.trigger: journal-level JIF used to infer an individual's quality
edge_cases.example: candidate ranked by the JIF of journals they publish in
edge_cases.detection_method: flag any use of a journal metric in an individual/article assessment
resolution: block journal-metric use at individual level
substitute article-level normalized impact with uncertainty

edge_cases.trigger: MNCS reported for a tiny publication set without intervals
edge_cases.example: MNCS=3.0 from 4 papers presented as decisive
edge_cases.detection_method: check sample size against stability threshold before reporting a mean indicator

edge_cases.trigger: units compared using metrics from different source databases
edge_cases.example: one unit measured in Scopus, another in WoS
edge_cases.detection_method: verify a single source basis across the whole comparison set
resolution: recompute all units on one source

edge_cases.trigger: viral or controversial attention inflates an altmetric composite
edge_cases.example: a retracted paper with a very high Altmetric score
edge_cases.detection_method: inspect attention source-type breakdown and sentiment for outliers
resolution: do not equate attention with quality

edge_cases.trigger: self-citation or citation-cartel activity inflates an indicator
edge_cases.example: an author's h-index inflated by coordinated self-citation
edge_cases.detection_method: run self-citation share and citation-network anomaly checks

edge_cases.trigger: interdisciplinary output assigned to a single field
edge_cases.example: a bioinformatics paper normalized only against biology
edge_cases.detection_method: audit field assignment for high interdisciplinarity cases

edge_cases.trigger: normalized value reported with no stated baseline
edge_cases.example: MNCS=1.4 reported without saying relative to what
edge_cases.detection_method: require an explicit baseline reference for every normalized value
resolution: restate value relative to the calibrated baseline

edge_cases.trigger: a single short window applied across fast and slow fields
edge_cases.example: 2-year window makes a math journal look low-impact
edge_cases.detection_method: compare window length against field citation-aging curves

edge_cases.trigger: results cannot be reproduced from documented inputs
edge_cases.example: a ranking that no one can regenerate from the stored package
edge_cases.detection_method: attempt an independent rerun from the reproducibility package

edge_cases.trigger: author name homonyms merged or a researcher's record split
edge_cases.failure_mode: wrong individual profile in a high-stakes decision
edge_cases.example: two same-named researchers merged into one profile
edge_cases.detection_method: audit disambiguation on a labeled sample and require ORCID where possible

edge_cases.trigger: a composite index hides which indicator drives the result
edge_cases.example: a single composite score conceals a weak validity component
edge_cases.detection_method: require constituent indicators and weights to be reported with any composite
resolution: prefer a profile over a composite

workflow.objective: fix the evaluation question, unit, comparison set, and window
acceptance_tests: unit, comparison set, window, and decision are all named
workflow.do_first_because: mis-scoping propagates to every downstream metric choice

gates: framework principles mapped to enforced rules
acceptance_tests: each adopted principle has an enforced indicator-use rule
workflow.do_first_because: use constraints must exist before any indicator is selected

workflow.objective: choose data source(s) and normalization basis
workflow.do_first_because: every count depends on source and normalization decisions

gates: baseline matched to unit and window
acceptance_tests: baseline documented and matched to the comparison set
workflow.do_first_because: normalized values are meaningless without a calibrated baseline

workflow.objective: compute the candidate indicators on the fixed foundation
gates: computations use the approved basis and source
acceptance_tests: all indicators computed on one consistent basis
workflow.do_first_because: indicators must be computed before validity, gaming, and uncertainty work

workflow.objective: assess validity of each candidate indicator against the target construct
gates: each indicator linked to a construct it validly measures
acceptance_tests: human review where validity is weak
workflow.do_first_because: only validated indicators may enter the portfolio

workflow.objective: assess gaming/Goodhart risk for high-stakes indicator uses
gates: gaming vectors enumerated per high-stakes indicator
workflow.do_first_because: gaming-resistant indicators must be chosen for high-stakes use

workflow.objective: assemble the fit-for-purpose indicator portfolio and broader-impact evidence
acceptance_tests: each indicator maps to a question facet
workflow.do_first_because: a balanced portfolio prevents single-metric distortion in the report

workflow.objective: attach uncertainty to each indicator and package for reproducibility
acceptance_tests: every reported indicator carries an interval
independent rerun reproduces results within tolerance
workflow.do_first_because: the report must not present point estimates without uncertainty or auditability

workflow.objective: produce the caveated, responsible-use-compliant evaluation report
acceptance_tests: every claim tied to the question
workflow.do_first_because: the report is the released artifact and must pass all validity, uncertainty, and review gates

dominance_rules.trigger: high-risk indicator use ready but report deadline pressure
dominance_rules.rule: validity, uncertainty, and review gates dominate schedule for high-stakes uses
dominance_rules.required_action: run validity, uncertainty, and human review before release
dominance_rules.example: do not publish an individual ranking before validity review

dominance_rules.trigger: a familiar but invalid/gameable metric is requested
dominance_rules.rule: indicator validity dominates recognizability or convenience
dominance_rules.required_action: drop or hard-guard indicators failing construct validity
dominance_rules.example: reject JIF as an author-quality proxy despite its familiarity

dominance_rules.trigger: stakeholders demand a single ranking for a high-stakes decision
dominance_rules.rule: responsible-use constraints dominate the demand for a single number
dominance_rules.required_action: provide a structured, caveated profile instead of one rank
dominance_rules.example: refuse a one-number league table for tenure

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value metric is ready before its foundation
dominance_rules.required_action: complete source and normalization foundations before computing dependent metrics
dominance_rules.example: do not compute MNCS before the normalization basis is fixed

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise score is desired but only heuristic grounding exists
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and avoid implying measured precision
dominance_rules.example: report a heuristic estimate, not a falsely exact coefficient

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is ready to lock but QA checks are incomplete
dominance_rules.rule: QA and acceptance tests dominate locking
dominance_rules.required_action: pass acceptance tests before any soft or hard lock
dominance_rules.example: do not hard-lock the report before uncertainty checks pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-stakes or contested use is detected
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automated decision for high-stakes/contested uses
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to a domain reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: flag an individual tenure decision based on metrics for human review

dominance_rules.trigger: adding a source improves coverage but breaks comparability
dominance_rules.rule: within a comparison, comparability dominates broader coverage
dominance_rules.required_action: use one consistent source/basis per comparison set
dominance_rules.example: do not mix Scopus and WoS within a single ranking

dominance_rules.trigger: a clean point estimate is requested for a small sample
dominance_rules.rule: uncertainty reporting dominates clean point presentation
dominance_rules.required_action: report intervals and small-N flags with every indicator
dominance_rules.example: show a wide CI for a 4-paper MNCS rather than a single number

dominance_rules.trigger: an indicator or claim is proposed without source grounding
dominance_rules.rule: source grounding and traceability dominate unsupported object creation
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence refs or exclude the claim
dominance_rules.example: drop an impact claim that has no contribution evidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not select or compute any indicator before the evaluation question and frame are fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: metrics chosen without a frame must be redone when the frame is defined
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: indicators computed but no approved scoping document exists
anti_rework_rules.example: computing MNCS before deciding the comparison set

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not finalize the indicator set before responsible-use constraints are set
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a non-compliant portfolio must be reassembled
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: portfolio assembled with no indicator-use policy
anti_rework_rules.example: selecting JIF for individuals before applying DORA

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not compute counts before the data source and its coverage are fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: counts on an unfixed source must be recomputed
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: metric values exist with no source decision record
anti_rework_rules.example: computing h-index before choosing WoS vs Scopus

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not compute normalized/percentile metrics before the normalization basis is fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: normalized values on a shifting basis must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: MNCS computed with no documented reference-set basis
anti_rework_rules.example: computing PPtop10% before defining field/year strata

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not interpret normalized values before the baseline is calibrated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: interpretations without a baseline must be revised
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: above/below-average claims with no stated baseline
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming MNCS=1.3 is 'strong' with no baseline

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not add an indicator to the portfolio before its validity is assessed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: invalid indicators must be removed and the portfolio rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: portfolio includes an indicator with no validity assessment
anti_rework_rules.example: including an altmetric as a quality proxy without validity evidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not deploy an indicator for high-stakes use before gaming risk is assessed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: gamed high-stakes results trigger costly reversals
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a high-stakes indicator has no gaming-risk record
anti_rework_rules.example: using h-index for promotion without self-citation checks

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not report indicators before uncertainty and stability are quantified
anti_rework_rules.rationale: point-estimate reports must be reissued with intervals
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: report shows ranks without uncertainty intervals
anti_rework_rules.example: publishing a league table with no confidence intervals

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hard-lock the report before reproducibility is verified
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an irreproducible released report cannot be defended
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: report hard-locked with no rerun verification
anti_rework_rules.example: releasing a ranking no one can regenerate

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not release high-stakes results before human review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: released high-stakes errors are hard to reverse
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: high-stakes report released with no human-review record
anti_rework_rules.example: releasing an individual assessment without expert sign-off

iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no material defects and no regression
